work.text: Several other pictures dated in the same or the previous year give a better idea of Tung's manner at the time of his richest [production]. … The usual motif of a [stream] winding between rocky mountains is beautifully developed in these pictures

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (The Later Ming and Leading Ch‘ing Masters)

moment.text: Men of former times Said: 'One must have brush and ink.' Many people do not understand the significance of these two words, brush and ink. But how could there be pictures without brush and ink?

source.author: Dong Qichang (Tung Ch‘i-ch‘ang)
source.title: Writings on painting
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (Lund Humphries, 1958; Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: The art of painting, which has been called ‘holding the Universe in the hand,' keeps constantly before the eyes the Works of Nature. … But where a laborious and minute technique is practised the painter becomes a slave of Nature, and she soon wears him out.
